title: 2017 MAZDA MX-5 Miata

highlights: Low mileage (24,800 mi) with single-owner history
6-speed manual, desirable Soul Red Metallic color
New tires and battery per seller
red_flags: Vehicle history report indicates accident or damage reported, contradicting seller's claim of flawless, pristine condition
normalized.prelim_summary: This 2017 Mazda MX-5 Miata Sport is a low-mileage, manual-transmission convertible in an attractive Soul Red Metallic finish, offered by a private seller in Napa, CA for $20,500. While the seller describes it as meticulously maintained with new tires and battery, the vehicle history report notes an accident or damage, which buyers should investigate further before purchase.

contradictions.detail: The seller describes the car as 'stunning, meticulously preserved', 'flawless' and in 'showroom condition', with no mention of damage. AutoCheck reports two collision events with bumper damage/repair (12/18/2020 and 09/21/2021). The tracker notes the damage disclosure was not carried into the current text.
The listing price is shown as $20,500, while the seller's own description states 'Asking Price: $19,500'.

critical_evidence.evidence: AutoCheck shows dealer 'recommended maintenance' entries in 2019 and 11/2024, but no reported entry between 07/2019 and 11/2024. No brake fluid flush or coolant service is itemised. The seller's 'freshly serviced' has no receipt.
There are no transmission records or door-jamb photo. AutoCheck dates manufacture to 08/2017, a late build that lowers early-6MT risk, but the gearbox condition is unproven.
Only an overhead view of the passenger footwell mat is provided; it looks dry on the surface. No lifted carpet, drain area or seat-rail photos.
AutoCheck Open Recall Check reads 'No Open Recalls', with recall service entries in 2019 and on 11/21/2024. Confirm with an NHTSA VIN lookup before purchase.
The battery photo shows a Super Start unit with an apparent 12/25 date sticker. The tires look fresh, but DOT dates are not legible and there are no receipts for tires, battery or service.

documentation.rationale: Identity is strong: VIN, VIN decode, an AutoCheck with one owner, clean title, smog pass and 11 dealer service entries. Maintenance proof is thin: there is a five-year reporting gap, no brake fluid or coolant by date, no receipts for the claimed fresh service and tires, and no repair documentation for two bumper damage events.

condition.rationale: Photos show clean paint, a tidy stock engine bay with no visible seepage, fresh-looking tires and an apparently new battery. Against that, two reported bumper collisions lack repair records. Underside, water pump, cabin water areas and the gearbox are not examined, and time-based fluids are undocumented.

price_value.rationale: $20,500 sits at the top of the profile's $17-20k California band for a 25k-mile 2017 Sport, before discounting two reported collisions and base trim. The deterministic fair value draws on pricier classes and roofs, so it overstates this Sport soft top.

mission_fit.rationale: This is a manual, low-risk ND within the ideal budget band and easy to resell, so it works as a bridge. However, the Sport trim is explicitly ruled out (cloth, no LSD), the soft top is the less preferred roof, and the 155 hp ND1 engine misses the ND2 plus.

logistics.rationale: Napa is a few hours' drive from Pacific Grove. A mobile PPI or a local Mazda dealer inspection is easy to arrange, the car is California-registered with a recent smog pass, and the PSX platform handles title and payment. Current availability needs confirming because the same VIN shows as sold on another listing.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Base Sport trim in red with black cloth hits three of Jason's explicit negatives: ruled-out trim, ruled-out colour and the least preferred interior. The only desirable trait is the manual gearbox, which is standard for the target.

ppi_focus: Paint meter on both bumpers, nose and rear quarters; check bumper mounts, reinforcement bars, headlight/taillight brackets and panel gaps for the 2020/2021 collision repairs
Warm-gearbox test: 2nd and 3rd synchro engagement, no grinding or popping out of gear, and diff whine
Clutch slip in 4th–6th under load, engagement height, and a hydraulic fluid leak check
Lift the carpet in both footwells; check soft-top drains, seat-rail bolts and floor connectors for water or corrosion
Soft-top fabric at the rear fold corners and header seal; do a water test if possible
Water pump weep hole, front crank seal, valve cover, and rear diff pinion and output seals
Read tire DOT dates and size, check for uneven wear, and do a battery load test
Check brake fluid moisture content and coolant condition, and do an OBD scan for stored codes
Suspension bushings and end links on the lift; alignment printout
what_would_change_verdict: Up: invoices showing professional bumper repairs plus a clean paint-meter PPI, together with dated fluid services and DOT-verified tires
Up: a price concession toward the Sport band to reflect the two reported collisions
Down: evidence of hidden structural repair, a mismatched respray beyond the bumpers, or water in the cabin
Down: confirmation that the car has already sold, or a refusal to allow a PPI
Down: gearbox grinding when warm or clutch slip at inspection
evidence.mission_note: A one-owner, late-build manual ND near home could serve as a low-risk pragmatic bridge. However, it is the ruled-out Sport trim in a ruled-out colour with a soft top, so it carries little of the point of view the enthusiast mission asks for.
evidence.rationale: The AutoCheck establishes identity and history well: one Napa owner since 10/2017, clean title, a late 08/2017 build, consistent mileage, no open recalls and a CA smog pass in 11/2025. It also establishes two minor collision events with bumper damage (12/2020, 09/2021). The seller's 'flawless, showroom' description omits these, and no repair documentation is offered. Reported dealer service clusters in 2019 and 11/2024, with no entries in between and no visible brake fluid or coolant service by date. The 'freshly serviced' claim is unsupported by receipts, and the 'premium' new tires are budget Sailun all-seasons with unreadable date codes. The photos show a stock, clean car with an apparently new battery and no visible engine bay seepage. The spec (Sport, Soul Red, black cloth, soft top) falls on Jason's ruled-out side, and the $20,500 ask sits at the top of the Sport band despite the damage history. Availability is also uncertain, because the same VIN shows as sold elsewhere.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller to confirm the car is still available and which price applies, and request the bumper repair invoices, DOT-date tire photos and the latest service invoice before arranging any inspection.
